newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T unit to buy back preference shares.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T unit to buy back preference shares.

text.p: British-American Tobacco Co Ltd said on Monday it planned to buy back certain preference share issues worth about 8.6 million stg at their proposed cancellation prices.

The company, a unit of tobacco and insurance group B.A.T Industries Plc, said it would buy back all of its outstanding five percent cumulative preference stock for 73.784p cash per unit and its six percent second cumulative preference stock for 88.187p cash per unit.

The terms represented increases of about 32 percent and 29 percent, respectively, on the closing mid-market prices of the five percent and six percent stocks on October 10, the company said in a statement.
British-American Tobacco is a unit of tobacco and insurance group B.A.T Industries Plc.
The company also proposed issuing 42 million new ordinary shares of 25p each at par to its immediate parent, British-American Tobacco (Holdings) Ltd, as part of the deal.
The new shares would be paid up by way of capitalisation of reserves, the company said.
The company expected the cancellation to become effective on December 12.
The company's board was advised on the payment terms by BZW.
